message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The genes that control mane development are typically expressed in a dominant fashion, meaning that if a male inherits the allele responsible for mane growth from either parent, it will manifest as a full or partial mane. This trait is not only visually striking but also plays a role in social signaling and mate selection within lion prides.
